minutes.headline: Planning Board waived site plan review for 305 Leominster Shirley Road and continued the Subaru dealership hearing to April 26.
minutes.summary: The Planning Board, with only three members present, heard an update on the 925 Mass Ave brownfield cleanup, opened the North End Subaru site plan hearing and continued it until after Zoning Board and Conservation review, and granted a site plan review waiver with two conditions for a contractor's yard at 305 Leominster Shirley Road. It also adopted its site plan and special permit rules, approved the prior minutes, and discussed parking calculations for takeout restaurants and camps.

attendees.name_as_heard: Bernie (land use director; also called Adam)

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none came.
Asked whether the warrant article on parking would affect the Mazda/Subaru dealership, thanked the owners for their service to the town, and asked to comment on parking later.

Asked for side-by-side examples of the proposed parking calculation, asked whether it would apply to Brooks House and other village sites, called the CVS parking an overkill, and voiced support for takeout windows such as Conrad's.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board granted a site plan review waiver for 305 Leominster Shirley Road, with conditions on sight distance and following the stamped plan.
The board continued the North End Subaru hearing at 757 Chase Road to April 26, to follow the Zoning Board and Conservation meetings.
The board approved its rules and regulations for site plan approval and special permits and closed that hearing, 3-0 by roll call.
On 925 Mass Ave, the town manager said a request for interest is coming and asked the board to weigh auction against a request for proposals.
The board leaned toward a parking rule of one space per three outdoor seats for takeout restaurants, to be edited at a public hearing.

why_it_matters: The 925 Mass Ave sale route and the unknown cleanup cost decide whether the town can find a private buyer for the site and what it may have to fund itself.

The Subaru hearing, the waiver for the contractor's yard and the proposed parking rule for takeout restaurants are land-use decisions that shape development on Chase Road and in village centers, and the parking change may reach a town meeting warrant.
watch_next: The Subaru hearing resumes April 26 at 6:30, after the Conservation meeting on April 7 and the Zoning Board meeting on April 14.
The Pierce tree farm agricultural preservation restriction, where the town's share is a fraction of the purchase price, is expected on the town meeting warrant.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the two non-procedural votes, the $30,000 Phase II grant and the $6,000 Phase III funds, apart from a caption comma error. They diverge on the Subaru continuance vote, which appears only in ours, and on the take-out parking and DLTA items, where ours records a lean or a decision and the official minutes do not. The official minutes also omit several budget figures and discussions we caught, and add the BrightFarms items and the absent members and public speakers that our minutes lack.
